title: Thunderbird mail profiles
whyItMatters: Each Thunderbird profile holds the local copy of mail folders, the address book, calendar and saved account passwords. It shows who the person corresponded with and often the content of the messages.
source: Mozilla Support, profiles: Thunderbird stores its profile folders in ~/.thunderbird on Linux: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profiles-where-thunderbird-stores-user-data
notes: Matches the profile folders themselves, so no mailbox contents are walked; profiles.ini in the same folder names them and is not counted. On Ubuntu 24.04 and later Thunderbird is usually the Snap, which uses ~/snap/thunderbird/common/.thunderbird instead, covered by a separate rule.

cleanup.exportFirst: Export the address book and calendars from Thunderbird, and copy the profile folder to a backup drive, before anything is removed.
cleanup.signOut: Remove the mail accounts in Thunderbird's account settings, so no saved password or login token for these mailboxes stays on the computer.
steps: Uninstall Thunderbird from the App Center if you are removing the app itself.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Deletes the local copy of all mail, address books, calendars and saved account passwords in those profiles. Mail kept on the server is not affected.
cleanup.source: Mozilla Support, Profiles - Where Thunderbird stores your messages and other user data: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profiles-where-thunderbird-stores-user-data
